streams.pump_role: Main feed for substrates and heterogeneous catalyst
streams.reasoning: Chemistry Plan specifies single stream with all reagents. Concentration matches batch (0.25 M). Flow rate derived from Analogy 1 (0.4 mL/min) adjusted for reactor sizing.

mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan requires pre-mixing all reagents and catalyst before heating. Static mixer ensures homogeneous distribution of heterogeneous Cu/C.
pre_reactor_steps: Suspend Cu/C in acetone with substrates to ensure wetting.
Filter suspension through 0.45 micron filter to remove large carbon aggregates if necessary, or use slurry pump capable of handling fine solids.
post_reactor_steps: Pass effluent through inline filter (0.2-0.45 micron) to remove Cu/C catalyst.
chemistry_notes: Reaction is Cu-catalyzed Huisgen cycloaddition. Heterogeneous Cu/C requires careful handling to prevent clogging; inline filtration is critical. High temperature (150 C) requires BPR. Analogy 1 (thermal cross-coupling) provides best hardware precedent for high-T flow. Residence time reduced from 3 min (batch) to 0.2 min (flow) based on kinetic intensification and analogy trends, though experimental verification is needed due to mass transfer limitations (Da >> 1).

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Calculation suggests 0.2 min (12 s) for 18x intensification. Analogy 1 used 10 min for similar thermal activation. Short time chosen to match kinetic potential, but risk of low conversion due to mixing limits (Da=289).
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Matches batch (150 C) and Chemistry Plan. Analogy 1 used 170 C, but 150 C is sufficient for batch yield.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Calculation requires 11.8 bar to keep acetone liquid at 150 C. Set to 12 bar. Analogy 1 used 10 bar at 170 C (MeCN), consistent with high pressure needs.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: Stainless Steel preferred for 150 C and potential abrasion from Cu/C. Analogy 1 used SS. FEP/PFA may degrade or soften at 150 C under pressure.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Matches batch (0.25 M). Analogy 1 used 0.65 M, but lower concentration helps mitigate clogging risk with heterogeneous catalyst.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Calculated from V = Q * t = 0.5 mL/min * 0.2 min = 0.1 mL. Small volume minimizes holdup of hazardous azide.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID used in Analogy 1 and Analogy 2. Balances pressure drop and clogging risk for slurry.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: Thermal cross-coupling in SS coil at 170 C, 10 bar BPR. Similar thermal regime and BPR requirement.
Analogy 2: Azide chemistry in PFA coil at 120 C. Confirms feasibility of azide flow, but lower T.
